verses.text: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's rule, Baasha king of Israel attacked Judah. He built up the town of Ramah so that no one could go in or out to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa took silver and gold from the treasures of the LORD's temple and of the king's palace. He sent it to Ben Hadad king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, with this message:

"Let's make a treaty between you and me, like there was between my father and your father. Look, I am sending you silver and gold. Go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so he will leave me alone."
Ben Hadad agreed with King Asa. He sent the commanders of his armies against the towns of Israel. They attacked Ijon, Dan, Abel Maim, and all the storage towns of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard about it, he stopped building Ramah and gave up the work.
Then King Asa brought all the men of Judah, and they carried away the stones and wood Baasha had been using to build Ramah. Asa used them to build up Geba and Mizpah.
At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "You trusted the king of Syria and did not trust the LORD your God. So the army of the king of Syria has escaped from you.
Weren't the Ethiopians and the Libyans a huge army, with chariots and very many horsemen? But because you trusted the LORD, he handed them over to you.
The LORD's eyes search all over the earth to give strength to those whose hearts are fully faithful to him. You have acted foolishly in this. From now on you will have wars."
Asa was angry with the seer and put him in prison, because he was furious with him about this. At that time Asa also treated some of the people cruelly.
Everything Asa did, from beginning to end, is written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, Asa got a disease in his feet. His disease was very bad, but even in his sickness he did not look to the LORD for help, only to doctors.
Asa died in the forty-first year of his rule.

They buried him in the tomb he had cut out for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bed covered with sweet-smelling spices and perfumes made by skilled perfume makers. And they made a very large fire to honor him.
